mutations.because: the 412 drain stops swallowing. The drain exists to put the connection back in the pool, and the store's answer — this key is taken, the exclusive create lost — is already in hand, so a drain that fails mid-stream means the connection is being torn down anyway, which is what the drain wanted. Unwrapped, a transport failure during it replaces "this asset already exists" with `S3RequestError`, and a caller that retries on a 500 re-uploads an asset that was never created. This is the ONE body read that must not be wrapped, and it is the exception that proves the four others are the rule rather than an oversight.

`get`'s body read is back outside any wrapper, and `send`'s `try` covers only the fetch PROMISE — `fetch` resolved when the status line arrived, so every byte after that was never covered. undici reports a connection dropped mid-body as `TypeError: terminated` whose `cause` is a `SocketError` carrying `socket: { remoteAddress, remotePort }`, so the raw rejection escapes carrying the internal host: a caller cannot tell a transport failure from a refusal, and the never-echo guarantee stops at the status line. Nothing in that chain is a STRING, which is why the test's walker reads own enumerable properties and not only `message`/`cause` — a message-only walk calls this clean while `10.99.7.3` sits in the object two links down. The same wrap is on `copy`, `list` and `fail`, each with its own failing-stream test.
